record.referenced_statement: For a finite compactly supported non-polar measure tau on a disk, a nonpositive Green potential a with ddc a=tau yields a bounded subharmonic v=exp(a) with tau << ddc v.
record.context_expansion: This is the n=1 substitute; Cegrell's n>=2 theorem is not used outside its dimension range. The Green potential a can be unbounded, and its negative-infinite locus is polar.
application_steps: The finite compactly supported measure has a genuine locally integrable nonpositive Green potential a.
For a_M=max(a,-M), the bounded chain inequality and locality imply ddc exp(a_M)>=1_{a>-M}exp(a)tau.
The bounded subharmonic functions exp(a_M) decrease to exp(a), hence their Laplacians converge distributionally; the positive right sides increase to exp(a)tau off the polar set.
Tau is non-polar, so exp(a)>0 tau-almost everywhere. Thus ddc exp(a)>=exp(a)tau implies tau<<ddc exp(a).
The normalization 1+exp(a) lies in [1,2]. No boundedness of a is assumed.
